subject: POC Capacity Planning - next steps & reserved GPU proposal
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@acmeai.com>, Priya Singh <priya@acme.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: POC Capacity Planning - next steps & reserved GPU proposal

Thanks for a productive call today - great to meet the Acme AI team. Per our discussion, summarizing the proposed POC goals, evaluation success criteria, timeline, and initial capacity plan so we can align on next steps. Please confirm or flag anything missing.

POC goals (2 weeks):
- Validate Redwood inference performance on your reranking + chat pipeline for typical customer load.
- Measure latency at p95/p99, token costs, and throughput with production prompts.
- Verify integration with your ingestion pipeline and secure logging (no customer PII stored in logs).

Success criteria (what you told us):
1) p95 latency < 300ms for single-shot rerank (avg prompt length ~120 tokens)
2) Throughput >= 3k requests/hour with <10% degraded responses
3) Cost per 1k tokens within 20% of your budget target
4) No data-exfiltration flags on security scan

Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize data/sample prompts and provide test keys.
- Week 1: run synthetic and production-sampled loadtests; measure latency/cost.
- Week 2: joint review, remediation (if any), and recommendation for reserved capacity.

Initial capacity ask from Acme (you):
- Target steady concurrency ~40 req/s, peak bursts to ~120 req/s for short windows.
- Average response length ~120 tokens; worst-case ~600 tokens for long-form debug runs.

Proposed POC capacity (high level):
- Reserved: 4x A100-80GB (dedicated) to guarantee baseline throughput for reranking workloads.
- Autoscale: add up to 2 additional GPUs when utilization >75% for >3 minutes; burst to on-demand up to 8 GPUs (2-3 hour daily allowance) for scheduled heavy tests.
- Caching & batching: we will enable prefix KV caching and adaptive batching to reduce per-token cost.

Attachments: I attached a capacity workbook (acme_poc_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx) with estimated qps/throughput numbers and a short reserved GPU proposal.

Next steps (action owners):
- Marissa (me): finalize SOW + reserved GPU quote (send by EOD tomorrow).
- Connor: create test plan and exact load profiles to run during Week 1.
- Acme: share sample prompts, 24h of request traces, and account for any internal redaction needs (Priya).

If that looks right, let's schedule a 30m kickoff for Monday to confirm the sample data and sign off on the workbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks, Marissa - this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side before Connor builds the test plan:

- The 40 req/s baseline is accurate for production-weighted traffic; peaks to 120 req/s happen during batch refreshes and occasional live demos (peaks generally last 5-10 minutes).
- Typical token counts: 120 tokens avg, 600 tokens long tail. For budget purposes assume 30% of calls are long-tail.
- We will provide a 24h trace dump and sanitized sample prompts by EOD Friday.

Capacity questions: can you confirm expected latency per request on the proposed 4x A100 baseline for both reranking and chat-style completions? Also, what's the expected time to scale from 4 -> 6 GPUs during the burst event (we care about warm-up time since some requests are latency-sensitive)?

Finally, Priya asked about the ability to limit burst usage to specific windows (we only want to allow it for scheduled tests).

Appreciate it - looking forward to Connor's plan.

- Ethan

Subject: Re: POC Capacity Planning - next steps & reserved GPU proposal

Hi Ethan / Priya - thanks for the details. Quick answers and an initial technical capacity plan below. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through numbers.

Latency expectations (approx, p95, under typical POC load profiles):
- Reranking (single-shot, 120 tokens): p95 ~180-240ms on 4x A100-80GB with adaptive batching and KV cache enabled.
- Chat-style (context + response, avg 120 tokens): p95 ~240-320ms depending on context length and KV cache hit rate.

Reserved + autoscale proposal (detailed):
- Baseline reserved: 4x A100-80GB (dedicated) - should cover steady 40 req/s with room for spikes.
- Autoscale policy: add 1x A100 at 75% avg GPU utilization sustained for 180s; add a second if >80% for another 180s.
- Burst policy: allow on-demand scale up to 8 GPUs for scheduled windows only (configurable windows in the Console). We recommend limiting unscheduled bursts; ops can require approval.
- Warm pool: pre-warm 1 GPU for scheduled tests (start 10 min before test start) to reduce cold-start latency.

Estimated scale times (approx):
- Cold start for an A100 instance (provision + model load): 90-180s depending on model and quantization.
- Warmed/preloaded instance: <15s to route traffic once container is ready.

Cost notes: reserved capacity price + on-demand burst costs will appear separately on the quote; workbook contains a cost sensitivity table based on your token mix.

Operational notes for POC:
- We'll run a short set of synthetic ramp tests day 1 to validate the autoscale thresholds and to tune batching.
- Connor / Laura will share the exact load profiles and a runbook (who to escalate to) before tests.

Attachment: updated_capacity_estimates.csv (inline in workbook).

Let me know if you want Connor/Dev/Laura to join the Monday kickoff to confirm scheduled windows and warm-pool settings.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Looping in some operational considerations from infra/SRE side:

1) Autoscale cooldowns & safety:
- Recommend a 3-5 minute cooldown after a scale event before allowing further scale actions to avoid oscillation.
- Implement health checks and gradual traffic shift when adding a GPU (drain/shift policy).

2) Warm pools & pre-warming:
- We can pre-warm up to 2 GPUs for scheduled tests, but this will incur reserved-on-demand charges for that window. We will document the cost trade-offs in the workbook.

3) Model warm-up:
- If you plan long-form runs (600 tokens), we recommend running a short synthetic warm-up sequence for pre-loading KV caches to lower first-request latency.

4) Rate-limiting & burst gating:
- We can enforce burst windows in Console and limit burst capacity to specific IPs/accounts if needed.

5) Ownership and runbook:
- Infra/Retail SRE (Dev) - responsible for scaling policy ops and alerts.
- Connor - test-plan and tuning during POC.
- Acme - provide sample traces and confirm redaction policy.

I'll prepare a short runbook (playbook for escalations and scale issues) and upload to the Drive link once ready. One question: do you require SOC2 evidence or specific audit logs during the POC? We can enable extended logging but need to confirm retention window.

- Dev Patel
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference
